appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais laisse-le donc où il est, il n'est plus là pour nous embêter. Crois-tu qu'il pleurnicherait, qu'il voudrait te mettre ton manteau, s'il te voyait là, la fenêtre ouverte, le vilain singe. »
appraisal_events.explanation: In what the narrator explicitly calls a ritual profanation, the friend crudely mocks and insults the dead Vinteuil in front of his own portrait, which Mlle Vinteuil has deliberately drawn attention to.

status_effects.explanation: Vinteuil is savagely mocked after his death, reduced to a contemptuous epithet ('le vilain singe') in a scene the narrator frames as ritual desecration of his memory.
Mlle Vinteuil is diminished by her own staged complicity, having drawn her friend's attention to the portrait as if by accident so as to provoke the profanation of her father's memory.

ambiguities: It is not fully certain whether Mlle Vinteuil consciously stages the portrait's visibility to invite the profanation or is driven by a more compulsive, half-acknowledged impulse; the narrator's framing as 'ritual' leans toward deliberate staging.
